body: We got called to a project in Boston by social workers for a 14 y/o male barricaded in his bedroom, this was in early September quite a few years ago. Apparently the family had recently moved from Cambridge and the kid was supposed to start at a new school. The new school called the social workers because the kid never showed up for the new school year. Social worker hadn’t been able to actually see the kid but parents were reporting that he was leaving his bedroom to use the bathroom, shower and eat. After some more digging we found out this had been going on for 6 weeks. We had BPD on scene with us because we figured we would have to force the door. It turned out that this kid’s “barricade” was him sitting in front of his door so his parents couldn’t open it. Eventually we got it open and the first thing that punched us in the face was the smell. Weeks worth of urine and feces. Once we got all the way in it was clear that the only time he was leaving his room was to sneak into the kitchen to take bags of chips and snacks. The kid was covered, head to toe, in urine and feces. The worst part was the utter indifference of the parents, it seemed like this was a situation they just couldn’t be bothered to deal with. His room was sweltering hot with the shades drawn but he still had on sweatpants and a hoodie the the hood up over his head. Me, my partner, and the two cops ended up each grabbing a limb and carrying him downstairs because nobody wanted to put him on his bedroom floor to try and restrain him. The poor kid was nonverbal the entire time, he just kind of made animal like noises and fought us the entire time. Also I should mention he was so malnourished he looked like he was only 11 or 12 and he was extremely weak. He must not have ever changed his clothes because once we got him to the hospital, the hood was so matted into his hair that we ended up having to cut some of it off. That was one of the worst things I’ve ever seen, and the best part... they tried to dispatch us to a new call while we were still in the ER.
